This vote was on accepting the Senate's changes, which sends the bill to the President. A Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Passage — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026 and provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds for certain community funding projects.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds to implement section 24220 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including any requirements enabling or supporting vehicle "kill switch" technology, and to prohibit federal spending for the execution or enforcement of such authorities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes (H R 7147)
votes.bill_title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security through May 22, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to financial services, general government, national security, the administration of foreign affairs, and foreign assistance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the National Endowment for Democracy.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to reduce the District of Columbia District and Appeals Court funding by 20% and to strike the salary and expense funding for Judges Boasberg's and Judge Boardman's staffs.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and extends various expiring programs and authorities. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Retaining Divisions B and C — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Divisions B and C. A Yea keeps them in the bill; a Nay would remove them.

votes.question: On Retaining Division A — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Division A. A Yea keeps it in the bill; a Nay would remove it.

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 11.12.26

Topic: Clinical Trials

https://t.co/ZSzHD6g4Wv

Agriculture supports local economies in Virginia’s Ninth District.

As part of an October farm tour, I visited Red Sun Farms in Dublin to learn about its ongoing greenhouse work and advanced technology. https://t.co/jMkIyqUN3R

During an October legislative breakfast, I enjoyed meeting with members of the Montgomery County School Board.

I wish local teachers, parents and students a positive few weeks of classes before Christmas break! https://t.co/wYLeU7eiJI
My Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act passes the House! https://t.co/c9OT4cNthl

On this Veterans Day, I voted for the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, which includes the Major Richard Star Act.

As a result, our nation’s veterans, their families and Gold Star families will access expanded benefits and opportunities. https://t.co/kncsBWqUaG

Thank you @caitlinnowens of Axios for the opportunity this week to discuss the landscape for Congress on health care policy.

I look forward to helping Republicans lead on solutions that help patients and rural communities. https://t.co/nlWelL0ZAT

As we honor Veterans Day, we also recognize the Ninth District military members and veterans who continue to serve our country. My District Director Cody Rush recently graduated from the U.S. Army Reserve Command and General Staff Officers’ Course. Congratulations, Cody! https://t.co/BRNe0909VO
https://t.co/XqFqgl4FTR

Under tough circumstances, @SpeakerJohnson helped guide a slim Republican majority to deliver policies that support freedom, prosperity and conservatism.

I thank Speaker Johnson for all he has done to help conservatives win, govern and advance the movement in DC.
Congratulations to the newly elected leadership for Republicans in the House. https://t.co/nMaDSjcGxT

Cut regulations ✅

Streamline licensing of nuclear energy projects ✅

Strengthen American producers of safe, reliable source of energy ✅

My bipartisan bill is on the House floor to accomplish these goals! https://t.co/vl1BsiNO1Z

This HHS announcement confirms that the Rural Health Transformation Program will continue to improve patient outcomes in rural Virginia.

An award for nearly $200 million will help yield health care access, resources and opportunity for rural communities in Virginia. https://t.co/EGmfDDDy0u

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 11.6.26

Topic: Veterans and Leadership

 https://t.co/2m1vca033q

The Radford Army Ammunition Plant helps serve U.S. military objectives.

Last month, I toured the Arsenal and engaged with leadership to support a critical partner for our military. https://t.co/41SN6rUpoE

Eastman Chemical provides local manufacturing jobs for Virginians at its sites in Henry County-Martinsville as well as at its Kingsport HQ.

In October, I toured Eastman’s HQ to see how the innovative recycling manufacturer supports our communities. https://t.co/co67Tvdrni

Floyd’s Huckleberry Dairy Farm is a family daily farm that has been around for more than a half-century.

I appreciate getting a firsthand look at their cattle and discussing policies to support local dairy farms and rural community family businesses. https://t.co/A8GbuclFuj

This year, the Martinsville Missile set a stock car land speed record of 253 miles per hour.

Today, I visited the Virginia Tech engineering department with leaders of the Martinsville Missile, Danny Turner and Joey Arrington, as they look to develop another record-shattering https://t.co/XnqcnmYcjB

VCHEC in St. Paul is a world-class clean coal facility that is a financial and environmental asset to our region. 

That is why I am calling for actions to protect VCHEC should Virginia regulators approve the proposed Dominion-NextEra Energy merger. https://t.co/VIUZJCfqcg

The ribbon-cutting and opening of the Cary C. Fuller Education Center presents new opportunities to recognize our region’s connection to First Lady Edith Bolling Wilson.

I enjoyed celebrating the October event with officials from the Wytheville - Wythe - Bland Chamber of Commerce before attending the group’s roundtable on local tourism.

Pamela Irvine is a great advocate for Southwest Virginia communities.

Her work leading Feeding Southwest Virginia inspires many to do the same.

I recently congratulated her on her retirement after 45 years and wished her well on her next endeavors. https://t.co/fcQlwwWgdM

My advocacy for Ninth District farms includes pushing federal agencies for crop relief.

During a recent farm tour with Virginia Farm Bureau officials, I visited a local Dublin farm to discuss the impacts of drought and overall farm policies. https://t.co/GmfUhpp7d2

Last week, I visited Carroll County for the J. Sidna Allen House Autumn Days.

In my DC office, I display a box that Allen made himself. My great-grandmother purchased it from Allen when she and her bible study group went to pray for Allen in prison a century ago. https://t.co/tMgsk1DGW4

October 24 is Dr. Pepper Day!

This Sunday, Rural Retreat is hosting an event to celebrate Dr Pepper’s roots right here in Southwest Virginia. https://t.co/CcTLI96QdG

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 10.23.26

TOPIC: Wagner

https://t.co/55k88VFyz1

Public health programs, resources and services are for patients, not fraudsters.

I am proud to be a Congressional leader in the War on Fraud. https://t.co/bN0yI0CiPc
The Faster Clinical Trials Act will expand research efforts, facilitate treatment options, and support American patients, particularly in rural America.

We're trying to bring the clinical trial to the patient instead of the model today of bringing the patient to the clinical trial.

https://t.co/Z4IILT4PCq

This past weekend, I delivered Congressional remarks to celebrate Billy Wagner the baseball player, but my speech at the ceremony was stories I had heard in Southwest Virginia about how good Billy Wagner the person is. A Tazewell park has been dedicated in his honor. https://t.co/yyuwEcqZ3V

Billy Wagner’s legendary path to the Hall of Fame started in Southwest Virginia.

But to our region, he is more than a generational athletic talent. He is a great human being. https://t.co/6JO4imCPkQ

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 10.16.26

TOPIC: Fighting for Coal

https://t.co/nFtnJp1lKy

While at my alma mater Emory & Henry University today, I signed Vice President Vance’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud.

From Medicare and SNAP fraud to fraudulent birth tourism, I will continue to be a leader in the War on Fraud. https://t.co/Xg3T2qN0OL

Republicans in Congress agree: fraudulently taking advantage of federal health care programs is WRONG!

Thank you Dr. Oz and @HHSGov for working to protect these benefits, stop fraud and support our vulnerable populations. https://t.co/Tgju5nsgcm

This month, I toured a faith-based addiction treatment center based in Floyd County.

As someone who has helped author policies to help combat substance use disorder, I will continue to promote related services and resources for patients. https://t.co/cHKYTuAmeJ

Auburn High School claims the Class 1 Virginia title in golf!

Congratulations on a stellar team finish! https://t.co/HGTllZQWlZ
https://t.co/IqAMbwndQl https://t.co/qnVARRQVkC

Graham High School’s golf program repeats as champs after winning the Class 2 state championship!

This is a remarkable accomplishment! https://t.co/RDq5B4muq1

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 10.9.26

TOPIC: Keeping Our Feet on the Ground and Reaching for the Moon

https://t.co/r2WRPwV2an

We recognize October 10, 1774, to honor our amazing history. 

Colonel Andrew Lewis led brave Western Virginians at the Battle of Point Pleasant.

Their actions opened the frontier, settlers moved west, forcing the British to cede territory to the U.S east of the Mississippi. https://t.co/S4xKYXDBiy

In my visit to Hillsville last week, I toured a local Saber Healthcare Group facility.

Thanks to the Hillsville Health and Rehabilitation Center for their time in discussing health issues with me. https://t.co/8edAA8ymfu
As part of my Thursday in Smyth County, I attended the local Chamber of Commerce Agricultural Dinner to celebrate those in the industry. https://t.co/NrLmNwynrI

In the aftermath of the October 7 attacks on men, women and children, I went to Israel with the U.S. Israel Education Association.

The pain and emotion from meeting survivors and hearing their stories still haunt me.

As we remember Oct. 7, support for our ally Israel remains. https://t.co/gcH9fFc8d8

Earlier this year, a Utility Trailer franchise opened a new facility at Seven Mile Ford in Smyth County.

On Thursday, I toured the facility with officials to learn more about how the company supports regional jobs. https://t.co/pT22Cp7Wq3

Last week in Smyth County, I participated with Governor Allen and Attorney General Miyares in a law enforcement roundtable.

Law enforcement officials from our region attended to share their perspectives and challenges. https://t.co/kPq2d19ise

Veterans who lose their medals can rely on my office to help recover replacements.

In September, I presented replacement medals, including a Purple Heart, to honor the Vietnam service of the late Gary Winebarger.

I presented the medals to his widow in Wise County. https://t.co/hf6JVgCK1C

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 10.2.26

TOPIC: Actions Against Fraud

https://t.co/OsBxsG293o

For the Bristol Chamber of Commerce September Coffee and Conversation, I sat down with Chamber and local officials.

I will continue to advocate for policies that support economic growth in our region. https://t.co/zbyaKzlRkn

I applaud @POTUS for prioritizing increased U.S. coal purchases by China. As an advocate for SWVA coal mining, I support negotiating tactics to have China purchase more American coal. This will help economic growth, protect coal jobs and provide certainty for coal operators. https://t.co/5c7phVWRMb

This month, I attended a ribbon-cutting for the Wildwood Recovery Center in Dickenson County.

As a chief sponsor of policies that address the synthetic opioid crisis, I will continue to support substance use disorder recovery measures. https://t.co/DYxig0C0ze

For too long, Medicaid fraud has cost American taxpayers and Medicaid beneficiaries.

Through this kind of action, we can improve fraud identification efforts and prevent foreign criminal actors from stealing valuable benefits that belong to patients. https://t.co/9E3BFJg6u3
States need to implement program integrity measures to protect our federal public health programs! https://t.co/kruY7t959e

Stop SNAP fraud.

SNAP benefits belong to the needy and vulnerable, not thieves. However, no system is currently in place to reimburse victims of SNAP theft, creating hardship for SNAP recipients.

I am proud to support a bill to protect SNAP recipients and punish fraudsters. https://t.co/DuEUYm8D4X

CONGRESSMAN GRIFFITH’S WEEKLY E-NEWSLETTER 9.25.26

TOPIC: Helene Revisited

https://t.co/pQw9Vanon0

I am proud to be a leading Virginia advocate for the AMLER program.

Thanks to AMLER, new cell towers will provide improved mobile communication on U.S. 460 between Buchanan and Tazewell Counties.

I recently spoke at a ribbon-cutting for this project! https://t.co/bpEQDXwyz5

One of the few remaining independently-owned hospitals in Virginia is Buchanan General Hospital in Grundy.

Last week, I toured the Hospital and discussed federal actions supporting rural health care. https://t.co/K3JuFsA7Id

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
